paragraphs.text: Cornelia de Lange syndrome-4 (CDLS4) is a cohesinopathy caused by mutation in RAD21, which encodes a structural protein of the cohesin complex. Affected individuals have growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features overlapping those of Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS), but much milder cognitive impairment than is seen in classic CdLS (Deardorff et al., 2012). Krab et al. (2020) described the phenotype as an attenuated form of CdLS compared with that caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, particularly for facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition, and behavior. Some patients have holoprosencephaly (Kruszka et al., 2019; Krab et al., 2020).

The mother of the first patient carried the same RAD21 deletion and had a history of melanoma and other unspecified medical problems.

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) reported 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations. The patients came from Australia, Europe, Turkey, Canada, and the United States, and 24 of the cases were previously unpublished. Full clinical information was available for 29 patients from 22 families (cohort A), aged 0 to 61 years, of whom 15 were male. All cohort A patients had CdLS scores of at least 5. Common features included: - short nose (23/26) - long and/or smooth philtrum (26/29) - concave nasal ridge (24/29) - thick eyebrows (20/24) - long eyelashes (21/26) - synophrys (19/28) - short fifth finger (23/28) - postnatal microcephaly (16/28) No patient had a major limb malformation. The following were less frequent than in the NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts: small hands (5/27), small feet (3/27), hirsutism (10/26), seizures (2/22), and visual impairment (0/24). Other findings were hearing loss (8 of 24), heart anomalies (9 of 23), gastroesophageal reflux (13 of 25), and cleft palate (6 of 25).

Self-injurious behavior and aggression were each seen in only 1 patient.

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) also summarized the natural history. Pregnancy and birth usually progressed normally, and prenatal growth retardation was uncommon. About half of the patients had congenital anomalies such as cleft palate or cardiac anomalies. Diaphragmatic hernia, anal atresia, and choanal atresia occurred occasionally. Short stature and microcephaly developed postnatally. Two unusual findings were relatively frequent in this series: vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut.

paragraphs.text: CDLS4 is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. Minor et al. (2014) described the first familial case, in which a RAD21 deletion was inherited from the mother. Boyle et al. (2017) found the same RAD21 deletion in an index patient and in her mother and 2 aunts, who did not meet the diagnostic criteria for CdLS. Based on their study and previous reports, Boyle et al. (2017) suggested that RAD21 variants are associated with incomplete penetrance and that carriers may therefore be underdiagnosed. Krab et al. (2020) found that variants were familial in 9 of 21 index cases in which inheritance could be determined. De novo mutations have also been reported (Gudmundsson et al., 2019; Krab et al., 2020).

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) identified 7 deletions that included RAD21. Six also removed neighboring genes. The seventh was a 27-kb deletion confined to RAD21 exons 1 through 9 (8q24.11). Patients with microdeletions tended to have higher CdLS scores and more frequent growth impairment than those with intragenic variants. However, the two groups did not differ in the frequency of major malformations or of cognitive and behavioral problems. In some patients with deletions, upper limb anomalies were likely caused by exostoses related to EXT1 haploinsufficiency.
